1	\section{Conclusion}
2	\label{sec:conclusion}
3	
4	We studied vision token pruning across seven VLA models (450M--7B) spanning three connector families on closed-loop robotic manipulation. Four findings emerge. (1)~The vision connector, not model scale or action head, determines pruning behavior along a four-class compressibility spectrum: uniformly critical (linear projection), threshold-graded (linear + deep post-processing), smooth graded (MLP), and catastrophic cliff (pixel-shuffle). The ordering is non-monotonic with parameter count; the monotonic CV-degradation relationship across all seven models, together with suggestive pairwise comparisons, points to the connector as the primary determining factor. (2)~Low-CV models are uniformly critical, not immune. $\pi_0.5$ retains 69.4\% success rate under random removal at $k{=}0.5$ but collapses to 33.4\% under L2 norm selection; this 36\,pp gap falsifies the ``immune'' interpretation from $\pi_0$'s offline-only evaluation and establishes that method selection, not just retention ratio, determines whether compression succeeds. (3)~Token importance CV serves as a zero-cost dual predictor: it forecasts both the tolerance class and the optimal pruning strategy from a single forward pass. The gap between random and L2 norm selection scales monotonically with CV at both $k{=}0.5$ and $k{=}0.7$, validated across three models. (4)~VTR re-encoding overcomes the catastrophic cliff: both cross-attention and parameter-matched MLP modules recover 60\%+ success rate at 75\% compression where all deletion methods yield 0\%, with a flat M-curve ($M{=}16 \approx M{=}128$).

1	\section{Results}
2	\label{sec:results}
3	
4	We evaluate token pruning across six VLA models spanning three connector families on LIBERO-Object~\cite{liu2023libero} (10 tasks, 50 episodes each, 500 total). All success rates report Wilson 95\% confidence intervals for single-seed results and mean $\pm$ standard deviation for multi-seed results.
5	
6	\subsection{Taxonomy Overview}
7	\label{sec:taxonomy_overview}
8	
9	Table~\ref{tab:taxonomy} organizes seven models into four response classes. The taxonomy reveals that effective vision-to-LLM pipeline complexity, not the nominal connector label or model scale, determines pruning tolerance. Token importance CV tracks this ordering continuously across an 8$\times$ parameter range (450M to 7B): uniformly critical models cluster at CV $< 0.06$, threshold-graded at $\sim$0.15, smooth graded at $\sim$0.22, and catastrophic cliff at $>$0.3. A pairwise comparison between $\pi_0$ and OpenVLA (both consuming 256 SigLIP-based~\cite{zhai2023siglip} tokens but differing in connector, backbone, and encoder fusion) yields a 63\,pp gap at $k{=}0.1$; this gap is consistent with the monotonic CV-degradation pattern across all seven models (Section~\ref{sec:linear_results}).
10	
11	The four classes differ qualitatively in their failure mode. Uniformly critical models ($\pi_0$, $\pi_0.5$~\cite{black2025pi05}) distribute importance so evenly that no scoring method can identify dispensable tokens; pruning either preserves random spatial coverage (and survives) or removes a clustered patch (and fails). Threshold-graded models (X-VLA) tolerate removal up to a sharp onset point. Smooth graded models (OpenVLA, OFT, CogACT) degrade proportionally to the fraction removed. Catastrophic cliff models (SmolVLA) collapse at any removal level.

\subsection{CV Correlates with Optimal Pruning Strategy}
\label{sec:scaling_law}

The preceding sections establish that connector architecture is strongly associated with pruning tolerance. A natural follow-up: can a single diagnostic indicate not only \emph{how much} pruning a model tolerates, but also \emph{which} strategy to use? Token importance CV provides this as a diagnostic metric that correlates with both pruning tolerance and optimal strategy. Table~\ref{tab:scaling_law} compares L2 norm-based and random removal at two retention ratios ($k{=}0.5$ and $k{=}0.7$) across three models with measured CV.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{L2 norm vs.\ random removal at two retention ratios. The gap $\Delta$(R$-$L2) scales monotonically with CV at both $k{=}0.5$ and $k{=}0.7$: low-CV models require random selection (uniform importance $\rightarrow$ L2 degenerates to spatial clustering), while high-CV models tolerate either strategy. The monotonic ordering holds across retention ratios despite a 2$\times$ change in token budget.}
\label{tab:scaling_law}
\begin{tabular}{lccccc}
\toprule
Model & CV & Tokens & L2 SR (\%) & Random SR (\%) & $\Delta$(R$-$L2) \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{6}{l}{\textit{$k{=}0.5$ (50\% retention)}} \\
$\pi_0.5$ & 0.055 & 768 & 33.4 & \textbf{69.4} & $+$36.0 \\
X-VLA & 0.151 & 50 & 43.4$\pm$0.8 & \textbf{70.3}$\pm$0.9 & $+$26.9 \\
OpenVLA & 0.215 & 256 & \textbf{39.2} & 37.4 & $-$1.8 \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{6}{l}{\textit{$k{=}0.7$ (70\% retention)}} \\
$\pi_0.5$ & 0.055 & 768 & 55.0 & \textbf{77.2} & $+$22.2 \\
X-VLA & 0.151 & 50 & 58.6$\pm$0.4 & \textbf{65.1}$\pm$0.1 & $+$6.5 \\
OpenVLA & 0.215 & 256 & \textbf{49.8} & 44.4 & $-$5.4 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

The gap decreases monotonically as CV increases at both retention ratios. At $k{=}0.5$: $+$36.0\,pp ($\pi_0.5$, CV$\,{=}\,$0.055) $\rightarrow$ $+$26.9\,pp (X-VLA, CV$\,{=}\,$0.151) $\rightarrow$ $-$1.8\,pp (OpenVLA, CV$\,{=}\,$0.215). At $k{=}0.7$: $+$22.2\,pp $\rightarrow$ $+$6.5\,pp $\rightarrow$ $-$5.4\,pp (OpenVLA, CV$\,{=}\,$0.215). The monotonic ordering holds across a 2$\times$ change in absolute token budget, strengthening the claim that CV captures a structural property of the connector rather than a coincidence at a single operating point.

The mechanism is intuitive. When tokens have near-uniform L2 norms (low CV), norm ranking captures spatial artifacts rather than genuine importance differences. L2 norm-based selection then clusters on correlated patches and loses spatial coverage, while random selection preserves the uniform distribution these models depend on. As CV rises, a genuine importance gradient emerges that L2 norm ranking can exploit; the random-vs-L2 advantage vanishes and eventually reverses.

CV therefore serves as a diagnostic metric that correlates with both tolerance and strategy. Low CV signals uniform criticality (sensitive to method choice but potentially robust under the right strategy), moderate CV signals a threshold or graded response, and high CV signals extreme fragility (catastrophic cliff). Models below CV $\approx 0.15$ should use coverage-preserving methods (random or spatially uniform selection), while models above this threshold can benefit from importance-based scoring.

At extreme compression ($k{=}0.3$), the interaction partially reverses for $\pi_0.5$: L2 norm achieves $53.2 \pm 3.1$\% (2 seeds) vs.\ random 36.4\% ($\Delta \approx -$17\,pp favoring L2). The optimal strategy also depends on the absolute token budget; when very few tokens remain, even spatially clustered high-norm tokens provide more signal than a sparse random sample. Full analysis of this interaction appears in Appendix~\ref{app:cv_strategy_interaction}.

1. **Vision token efficiency** — DynamicViT, EViT, ToMe, FastV, PruMerge, TokenPacker

### 扩展要求

**A. 需要搜索并新增的引用方向（用 WebSearch 查找 arXiv 论文）**：

### 论文上下文
这篇论文研究 VLA 模型中 vision token pruning 的效果。核心发现：
- Vision connector 架构与 pruning 行为强相关（4 类：uniformly critical, threshold-graded, smooth graded, catastrophic cliff）
- Token importance CV（L2 norm 的变异系数）作为零成本诊断指标，与 tolerance class 和最优策略相关

- 7 个 VLA 模型（450M-7B），3 种 connector 家族，4 个闭环评估 + 3 个离线/文献分析

- 新引用必须与论文主题相关（token pruning, VLA efficiency, vision connectors, closed-loop evaluation）

1	\section{Conclusion}
2	\label{sec:conclusion}
3	
4	We studied vision token pruning across seven VLA models (450M--7B) spanning three connector families on closed-loop robotic manipulation. Four findings emerge. (1)~The vision connector is strongly associated with pruning behavior along a four-class compressibility spectrum: uniformly critical, threshold-graded, smooth graded, and catastrophic cliff. The monotonic CV-degradation relationship across all seven models is consistent with the connector being a primary factor, though confounded by backbone differences. (2)~Low-CV models are uniformly critical, not immune: $\pi_0.5$ shows a 36\,pp gap between random and L2 norm selection at $k{=}0.5$, demonstrating that offline pruning tolerance does not guarantee closed-loop robustness. (3)~Token importance CV serves as a zero-cost diagnostic metric that correlates with both tolerance class and optimal strategy from a single forward pass. (4)~Learned re-encoding (both cross-attention and MLP, $p = 0.15$) recovers 60\%+ SR at 75\% compression where all deletion methods yield 0\%.
5	
6	These results yield a diagnostic protocol. First, compute CV from a single forward pass. Models below CV $\approx 0.15$ should use coverage-preserving methods; models above can use importance-based scoring; pixel-shuffle architectures require learned re-encoding. All closed-loop results use LIBERO simulation; $\pi_0$ evaluation is offline only; the CV correlation spans three models and two retention ratios. Code and evaluation scripts will be released upon publication.

14	
15	We study vision token pruning across seven VLA models (450M--7B) spanning three connector families on LIBERO~\cite{liu2023libero}, evaluating four in closed-loop and analyzing three via offline metrics or literature. The vision connector is strongly associated with pruning behavior along a four-class spectrum, and the coefficient of variation (CV) of token L2 norms correlates with both the tolerance class and the optimal strategy from a single forward pass. A central finding: low-CV models are not immune to pruning but \emph{uniformly critical}. Closed-loop evaluation of $\pi_0.5$~\cite{black2025pi05} (CV$\,{=}\,$0.055) reveals a 36\,pp gap between random and L2 norm selection at $k{=}0.5$, demonstrating that models showing offline pruning tolerance can exhibit severe closed-loop degradation when the pruning method introduces spatial bias. CV provides a zero-cost diagnostic: a single forward pass replaces hundreds of expensive closed-loop episodes.

6	\subsection{Taxonomy Overview}
7	\label{sec:taxonomy_overview}
8	
9	Table~\ref{tab:taxonomy} organizes seven models into four response classes. The taxonomy reveals that effective vision-to-LLM pipeline complexity, not the nominal connector label or model scale, is strongly associated with pruning tolerance. Token importance CV tracks this ordering continuously across an 8$\times$ parameter range (450M to 7B): uniformly critical models cluster at CV $< 0.06$, threshold-graded at $\sim$0.15, smooth graded at $\sim$0.22, and catastrophic cliff at $>$0.3. A pairwise comparison between $\pi_0$ and OpenVLA (both consuming 256 SigLIP-based~\cite{zhai2023siglip} tokens but differing in connector, backbone, and encoder fusion) yields a 63\,pp gap at $k{=}0.1$; this gap is consistent with the monotonic CV-degradation pattern across all seven models (Section~\ref{sec:linear_results}).
10	
11	The four classes differ qualitatively in their failure mode. Uniformly critical models ($\pi_0$, $\pi_0.5$~\cite{black2025pi05}) distribute importance so evenly that no scoring method can identify dispensable tokens; pruning either preserves random spatial coverage (and survives) or removes a clustered patch (and fails). Threshold-graded models (X-VLA) tolerate removal up to a sharp onset point. Smooth graded models (OpenVLA, OFT, CogACT) degrade proportionally to the fraction removed. Catastrophic cliff models (SmolVLA) collapse at any removal level.
